root.claim: One deterministic fixed-alphabet multitape Turing machine computes the exact product of two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, disproving the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture in that model.

motivation.text: The Harvey-van der Hoeven route already reduces multiplication to transform levels made of address rearrangements, signed shifts and butterflies; scanning all data per level costs n log n, so beating it needs savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The exponent $1-\kappa$ is strictly below one, so the bound beats $n\log n$ by a power of $\log n$, which the conjectured lower bound forbids.
